One day an elder sister came from town to visit her younger sister, who lived in a village with her husband. <break time="0.8s" /> Drinking tea together, the elder sister began to boast about the town, where people dressed well and ate fine food. <break time="0.8s" /> The younger sister did not like this, and she said that she would never change her life for her sisters. <break time="0.8s" /> Our life may be rough, but we are never anxious, and we always have enough to eat, she said proudly. <break time="0.8s" /> You town people may be rich today, but tomorrow you could lose everything and end up on the street. <break time="0.8s" /> The elder sister laughed and answered that peasants lived in dirt all their lives and died in it, too. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom, the master of the house, was lying on top of the stove, where he listened to the womens talk. <break time="0.8s" /> It is true, he thought, we peasants are too busy with our work to think of any nonsense. <break time="0.8s" /> Our only trouble is that we have too little land, and if I had plenty of land, I would not fear the Devil himself. <break time="0.8s" /> The Devil, who had been sitting behind the stove, heard everything and decided to give Pahom land and to trap him through it.

어느 날. <break time="0.8s" /> 언니가 도시에서 왔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 동생을 찾아보려고. <break time="0.8s" /> 동생은 남편과 함께 시골 마을에 살았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 함께 차를 마시며. <break time="0.8s" /> 언니는 도시 자랑을 늘어놓기 시작했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그곳에서는 사람들이 옷을 잘 입고 좋은 음식을 먹었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 동생은 이 말이 못마땅했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 말했다 자기 삶을 절대 바꾸지 않겠다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 언니의 삶과는. <break time="0.8s" /> 우리 삶은 거칠지도 몰라. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 우리는 걱정이 없어. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 늘 먹을 것이 넉넉해. <break time="0.8s" /> 동생이 자랑스럽게 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 너희 도시 사람들은 오늘은 부자일지 몰라. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 내일은 모든 것을 잃을 수도 있어. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 길거리에 나앉을 수도 있지. <break time="0.8s" /> 언니는 웃으며 대답했다 농부들은 평생 흙먼지 속에서 살고. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 속에서 죽기도 한다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 집주인인 파홈은. <break time="0.8s" /> 난로 위에 누워 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그곳에서 그는 여자들의 이야기를 들었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 맞는 말이야. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 생각했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 우리 농부들은 일하느라 너무 바빠서. <break time="0.8s" /> 쓸데없는 생각을 할 틈이 없지. <break time="0.8s" /> 우리의 유일한 문제는 땅이 너무 적다는 거야. <break time="0.8s" /> 만약 내게 땅이 넉넉하다면. <break time="0.8s" /> 악마조차 두렵지 않을 텐데. <break time="0.8s" /> 악마가 난로 뒤에 앉아 있었는데. <break time="0.8s" /> 모든 말을 들었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 파홈에게 땅을 주기로 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그 땅으로 그를 덫에 빠뜨리기로.

Near the village. <break time="0.8s" /> Lived a lady, a small landowner. <break time="0.8s" /> Who owned about three hundred acres. <break time="0.8s" /> She hired an old soldier. <break time="0.8s" /> As her manager. <break time="0.8s" /> Who fined the peasants. <break time="0.8s" /> Whenever their animals wandered onto her fields. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom paid many fines. <break time="0.8s" /> And each time he went home. <break time="0.8s" /> In a bad temper. <break time="0.8s" /> Shouting at his family. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the news came. <break time="0.8s" /> That the lady wanted to sell her land. <break time="0.8s" /> And the peasants all wished to buy some. <break time="0.8s" /> Because the Devil made them quarrel. <break time="0.8s" /> They could not buy it together. <break time="0.8s" /> So each man bought what he could. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom sold a colt and half of his bees. <break time="0.8s" /> Borrowed money from his brother in law. <break time="0.8s" /> And bought forty acres. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom was full of joy. <break time="0.8s" /> On the day when he first plowed his own fields. <break time="0.8s" /> And even the grass looked different. <break time="0.8s" /> But soon the neighbors cattle. <break time="0.8s" /> Began to stray into his meadows. <break time="0.8s" /> And Pahom began to take their owners to court. <break time="0.8s" /> Once he had been the poor man. <break time="0.8s" /> Who paid fines. <break time="0.8s" /> But now he was the one. <break time="0.8s" /> Who made others pay. <break time="0.8s" /> His neighbors grew angry. <break time="0.8s" /> And when someone cut down his lime trees. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom blamed a peasant named Simon. <break time="0.8s" /> Without any proof.

Near the village lived a lady, a small landowner, who owned about three hundred acres. <break time="0.8s" /> She hired an old soldier as her manager, who fined the peasants whenever their animals wandered onto her fields. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom paid many fines, and each time he went home in a bad temper, shouting at his family. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the news came that the lady wanted to sell her land, and the peasants all wished to buy some. <break time="0.8s" /> Because the Devil made them quarrel, they could not buy it together, so each man bought what he could. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom sold a colt and half of his bees, borrowed money from his brother in law, and bought forty acres. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom was full of joy on the day when he first plowed his own fields, and even the grass looked different. <break time="0.8s" /> But soon the neighbors cattle began to stray into his meadows, and Pahom began to take their owners to court. <break time="0.8s" /> Once he had been the poor man who paid fines, but now he was the one who made others pay. <break time="0.8s" /> His neighbors grew angry, and when someone cut down his lime trees, Pahom blamed a peasant named Simon without any proof.

마을 근처에. <break time="0.8s" /> 작은 땅 주인인 한 부인이 살았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀는 약 300에이커를 가지고 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀는 나이 든 군인을 고용했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 관리인으로. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 농부들에게 벌금을 물렸다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그들의 가축이 그녀의 밭에 들어올 때마다. <break time="0.8s" /> 파홈은 벌금을 여러 번 냈다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그때마다 집에 갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 몹시 화가 난 채로. <break time="0.8s" /> 가족에게 소리를 지르면서. <break time="0.8s" /> 그러다 소식이 들려왔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 부인이 땅을 팔려고 한다는. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 농부들은 모두 조금씩 사고 싶어 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 악마가 그들을 다투게 만들었기 때문에. <break time="0.8s" /> 그들은 그 땅을 함께 살 수 없었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 저마다 살 수 있는 만큼 샀다. <break time="0.8s" /> 파홈은 망아지 한 마리와 벌의 절반을 팔았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 처남에게 돈을 빌렸다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 40에이커를 샀다. <break time="0.8s" /> 파홈은 기쁨으로 가득했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 자기 밭을 처음 갈던 날. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 풀마저 달라 보였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 곧 이웃들의 소가. <break time="0.8s" /> 그의 풀밭으로 들어오기 시작했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그러자 파홈은 소 주인들을 고소하기 시작했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 한때 그는 가난한 사람이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 벌금을 내는. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 이제 그가 바로 그 사람이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 남에게 돈을 물리는. <break time="0.8s" /> 이웃들은 화가 났다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 누군가 그의 보리수나무를 베어 가자. <break time="0.8s" /> 파홈은 시몬이라는 농부를 탓했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 아무 증거도 없이.

One day a traveling peasant. <break time="0.8s" /> Told Pahom about a place. <break time="0.8s" /> Beyond the Volga. <break time="0.8s" /> Where each man received twenty five acres. <break time="0.8s" /> The land there was so rich. <break time="0.8s" /> He said. <break time="0.8s" /> That the rye grew as tall as a horse. <break time="0.8s" /> Why should I suffer. <break time="0.8s" /> In this narrow place. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom thought. <break time="0.8s" /> If I could live so well over there. <break time="0.8s" /> So he sold his land. <break time="0.8s" /> And moved his family to the new place. <break time="0.8s" /> Where they got a hundred and twenty five acres. <break time="0.8s" /> He was ten times better off than before but after a while. <break time="0.8s" /> Even this land did not seem enough. <break time="0.8s" /> He wanted to grow more wheat. <break time="0.8s" /> So he rented extra land every year. <break time="0.8s" /> Which often led to quarrels. <break time="0.8s" /> If the land were my own. <break time="0.8s" /> He thought. <break time="0.8s" /> I would be free. <break time="0.8s" /> And there would be no more trouble. <break time="0.8s" /> A peasant agreed to sell him. <break time="0.8s" /> Thirteen hundred acres for fifteen hundred rubles. <break time="0.8s" /> And the deal was almost settled. <break time="0.8s" /> Just then. <break time="0.8s" /> A passing dealer told him about the Bashkirs. <break time="0.8s" /> A simple people living far away. <break time="0.8s" /> He said that he had bought thirteen thousand acres from them. <break time="0.8s" /> For only a thousand rubles.

어느 날 떠돌이 농부가. <break time="0.8s" /> 파홈에게 어떤 곳에 대해 이야기해 주었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 볼가강 너머에 있는. <break time="0.8s" /> 그곳에서는 남자마다 25에이커씩 받았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그곳 땅은 아주 기름졌다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그의 말로는. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 호밀이 말 키만큼 자랐다. <break time="0.8s" /> 내가 왜 고생해야 하지. <break time="0.8s" /> 이 좁은 곳에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 파홈은 생각했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 저기서 그렇게 잘 살 수 있다면 말이야. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 그는 땅을 팔았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 가족을 데리고 새 곳으로 이사했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그곳에서 그들은 125에이커를 얻었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 전보다 열 배나 형편이 나아졌다 하지만 얼마 지나자. <break time="0.8s" /> 이 땅조차 충분해 보이지 않았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 밀을 더 기르고 싶었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 해마다 땅을 더 빌렸다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그런데 그 일로 자주 다툼이 생겼다. <break time="0.8s" /> 땅이 내 것이라면. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 생각했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 나는 자유로울 텐데. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 더는 골치 아픈 일도 없을 텐데. <break time="0.8s" /> 한 농부가 그에게 팔기로 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 1, 300에이커를 1, 500루블에. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 거래가 거의 성사되었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 바로 그때. <break time="0.8s" /> 지나가던 상인이 그에게 바시키르족 이야기를 해 주었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그들은 멀리 사는 순박한 민족이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 말했다 자기가 그들에게서 1만 3천 에이커를 샀다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 겨우 1, 000루블에.
